primary_metric: deps.dev directDependentCount summed over every Maven release
uncertainty: Eight verified Java SQL paths after a bounded Maven Central search (three queries, 143 hits) and deps.dev direct dependents summed over releases for 11 targeted leads, captured 2026-11-17, extended in round 2 with 14 more coordinates by the same function (Hive, Flink, Spark, ShardingSphere renames, ZetaSQL, Calcite Babel and others). org.jooq:jooq 3.21.9 (4,574), com.alibaba:druid 1.2.28 (1,945), com.facebook.presto:presto-parser 0.300 (1,453), org.apache.calcite:calcite-core 1.42.0 (1,250), org.apache.hive:hive-exec 4.2.1 (1,146), com.github.jsqlparser:jsqlparser 5.4 (950), org.apache.spark:spark-catalyst_2.12 3.5.9 (529) and io.trino:trino-parser 484 (525) parse both valid controls into their own trees, which give the oracle summary. The metrics mostly count other uses for jOOQ (query builder), Druid (JDBC connection pool), Calcite (planner and adapters), hive-exec (Hive's execution engine) and spark-catalyst (Spark SQL's analyzer and optimizer), and every value is summed over releases. presto-parser and trino-parser share the Presto/Trino SqlBase grammar ancestry (distinct packages and diverged sources). trino-parser and hive-exec have no public statement splitter, so their adapters remove the terminating semicolon; trino-parser, hive-exec and spark-catalyst parse one statement, so statement_count is 1 by API contract. Spark's catalyst API is published but marked internal, and its parser rewrites COUNT(*) to count(1), whose synthesized literal is excluded by its origin span. Hive's coverage sources are regenerated with ANTLR 3.5.2 from the pinned grammars and checked against the shipped line tables. The Calcite, Hive and Spark paths pin only the jars their parser paths load. Other leads are unverified, so this is not a top-ten ranking. java.sql has no SQL parser. Two valid controls establish only the tested dialect-neutral subset.
